faq.q: What are safe ways to show my feelings?
faq.a: Use your words, draw or write about it, cry, hug a pillow or a soft toy, move your body, or talk to a grown-up you trust. These let feelings out without hurting anyone.
asks: How can I show I am angry safely?

faq.q: Why is hitting not okay when I am angry?
faq.a: Hitting hurts other people and can make them scared or sad. It also does not fix the problem. Your anger is okay; using words or moving away is the safe choice.
asks: Why can I not hit when I am cross?

faq.q: How do I say what I feel?
faq.a: Try the magic sentence: "I feel... because... I need..." For example, "I feel sad because nobody played with me. I need a friend to play with."
asks: What are the right words for feelings?

faq.q: Is it okay to cry at school?
faq.a: Yes. Crying is a safe way to let feelings out. If you are upset at school, you can tell your teacher, who can help.
asks: What if I cry in class?

faq.q: What if I already did something unsafe?
faq.a: Everyone makes mistakes. Calm down first, then say sorry and help fix things. Next time, try one of the safe ways sooner.
asks: I hit my friend, what now?

facts: The term art therapy was first used by British artist Adrian Hill in 1942, after he found that drawing helped him recover while ill.
Psychologists call sentences like "I feel... because... I need..." I statements, and they help people share feelings without blaming.
